Analysis: Both hypotheses present innovative mechanistic frameworks linking ECM stiffness to tumor-associated macrophage function, but they differ in their balance of novelty, plausibility, testability, and safety. Hypothesis 2 is particularly novel because it couples mechanical cues with metabolic reprogramming and immune checkpoint regulation (PD‐L1 expression), integrating advanced bioengineering and gene-editing techniques. However, its increased complexity makes it harder to test reliably and raises concerns regarding safety due to the reliance on gene-editing methods and less mature intervention strategies. In contrast, Hypothesis 1, while slightly less expansive in novelty, offers a more plausible and straightforward mechanism with a clear feed-forward loop linking ECM stiffness to macrophage polarization and subsequent matrix remodeling. The proposed therapeutic interventions (utilizing integrin/FAK inhibitors and possibly YAP/TAZ modulators) are more in line with existing pharmacological strategies, thereby enhancing testability and minimizing potential safety risks. Overall, the balance of straightforward mechanistic clarity, feasibility in experimental design, and safer therapeutic targeting makes Hypothesis 1 the superior option.
